question: Do pretrained Transformers spontaneously organize function-specialized feed-forward neurons into causally meaningful modules, and when does that organization emerge during pretraining?

key_findings.claim: Pretraining produces neuron-level specialization across semantic, factual-knowledge, and downstream-task functions.
key_findings.evidence: The authors score individual FFN neurons by average precision on hundreds of binary sub-functions and compare pretrained T5/Switch checkpoints with randomly initialized counterparts; top-predictivity neurons are substantially more function-selective after pretraining.

key_findings.claim: Both native sparse experts and post-hoc partitions contain more functionally concentrated neurons than random partitions.
key_findings.evidence: At a 0.001 hypothesis-test threshold, Table 1 reports higher functional-expert proportions and modularization degrees for pre-MoE Switch and post-MoE T5 than random partitions. For example, post-MoE T5 task experts have proportion 0.120 and degree 3.276 versus 0.007 and 0.221 under random partitioning.

key_findings.claim: Targeted expert perturbations provide causal evidence, but the effect depends strongly on the perturbation design.
key_findings.evidence: For dense T5, perturbing function-ranked experts in the last four layers can reduce average accuracy by nearly 30% at 10% expert perturbation and outperforms matched neuron perturbations above 6%. For Switch, excluding functional experts reduces seven-task average accuracy from 73.23 to 72.78, while selecting only them reaches 74.45 after task fine-tuning.

key_findings.claim: Expert-level functional organization stabilizes earlier than individual-neuron rankings.
key_findings.evidence: Across pretraining checkpoints, expert predictivity rankings reach Spearman stabilization score 0.9 after about 15% of steps, versus roughly 75% for neurons; Switch shows a notable fluctuation around 20K steps and stabilizes more slowly than dense T5.

key_findings.claim: The evidence establishes MoE as one useful modular view, not a unique decomposition of Transformer computation.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly limits its search to equal-sized MoE-style groups and acknowledges that other module sizes, overlapping structures, and function taxonomies remain unexplored.

method.core_idea: Operationalize modularity as function-specialized neurons that are statistically concentrated and causally cooperative inside experts.
method.mechanism: Estimate neuron and expert predictivity on semantic, knowledge, and task sub-functions; flag functional experts with a binomial approximation to hypergeometric enrichment; compare native/pre-partitioned MoE, post-hoc MoEfication, random partitions, and random initialization; perturb expert routing or activations; then track rank correlations across pretraining checkpoints.
assumptions: Average precision on selected probes is a valid proxy for neuron function.
Top-one-percent neurons and a p<0.001 enrichment test meaningfully delineate specialization.
MoE expert boundaries are a plausible candidate module structure.
Targeted perturbation effects reflect functionally cooperative modules rather than distribution shift alone.
The selected semantic, knowledge, and GLUE tasks adequately sample model functions.

techniques.role: Scores individual FFN neurons on labeled sub-functions.
Tests whether high-predictivity neurons cluster within expert boundaries.
Tests causal importance by modifying dense activations or sparse routing.
Tracks coarse expert and fine neuron organization through pretraining.
Separates native sparse experts from post-hoc partitions of a dense model.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained and random T5/Switch Transformer FFNs
evaluations.result: MoE-aware partitions concentrate functional neurons more strongly than random partitions

evaluations.setting: Dense T5 on seen and unseen classification tasks
evaluations.metric: Average accuracy after matched expert or neuron perturbation
evaluations.result: Function-ranked expert perturbations are more damaging than neuron perturbations above 6% and can approach random performance
evaluations.baseline: Random, single-task, and average-predictivity neuron perturbations

evaluations.setting: Switch Transformer on seven GLUE tasks
evaluations.result: Original 73.23, excluding functional experts 72.78, selecting only functional experts 74.45
Expert rankings reach 0.9 around 15% of training, neuron rankings around 75%

limitations: The analysis considers MoE-style, mostly equal-sized, non-overlapping partitions rather than searching broadly over modular decompositions.
Function labels come from a limited task suite and may conflate correlation, selectivity, and causal necessity.
Dense-T5 and sparse-Switch perturbations are different and cannot be compared quantitatively.
Switch functional-only routing is followed by task fine-tuning, which can compensate for ablation.
The binomial approximation and top-one-percent cutoff are methodological choices rather than identified ground truth.
Claims about analogy to biological modularity are suggestive, not neuroscientifically validated.
failure_modes: A different probe distribution reassigns neuron functions and expert labels.
Highly polysemantic neurons make top-predictivity grouping look modular while sharing unrelated functions.
Noise injection or routing exclusion creates off-manifold activations that exaggerate causal effects.
Overlapping or hierarchical modules are missed by the fixed expert partition.
Fine-tuning after routing restriction masks the immediate cost of removing nonfunctional experts.
Early rank stability fails to imply that representations or behaviors have stabilized.
reusable_insights: Combine selectivity, enrichment, perturbation, and developmental timing rather than treating any one as sufficient evidence of modularity.
Use random partitions and random initialization as distinct null models.
Track module identity over training with rank-based measures that tolerate scale drift.
Audit perturbations for matched parameter count and off-distribution effects.
Treat discovered modules as hypotheses that should generalize to held-out functions and alternative decompositions.
open_questions: Do overlapping, unequal, or hierarchical module searches recover stronger and more stable functional structure?
Does expert modularity predict transfer, edit locality, compositionality, or robustness on held-out domains?
Can interventions that preserve activation distributions isolate module causality more cleanly?
Why does dense T5's post-hoc structure stabilize faster than native Switch routing?
How stable are modules across seeds, scales, languages, and modern decoder-only models?

competitive_landscape.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
competitive_landscape.difference: Switch establishes efficient top-one expert routing and documents training instability; the reviewed paper asks whether its expert boundaries also align with emergent functions and compares them with post-hoc dense partitions.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
competitive_landscape.difference: Geva et al. interpret individual FFN entries as pattern-to-vocabulary memories. This paper moves from individual units to statistically enriched expert groups spanning semantic, knowledge, and task functions.

competitive_landscape.title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Dai et al. identify and edit neurons associated with factual recall. The reviewed work includes factual probes but centers on whether specialized neurons group into modules and when that grouping stabilizes.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Upcycling: Training Mixture-of-Experts from Dense Checkpoints
competitive_landscape.difference: Sparse Upcycling converts trained dense checkpoints into MoE models to improve training efficiency. This paper's early dense modularity and post-MoE results offer a mechanistic hypothesis for why dense-first conversion may work, without testing upcycling performance itself.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Pretrained Transformers exhibit neuron specialization, function-based grouping within MoE experts, and a coarse-to-fine training process in which expert organization stabilizes before neuron functions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The work joins three probe families, enrichment tests, two distinct model/partition regimes, targeted interventions, and checkpoint trajectories.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The multi-level, temporal modularity audit is a useful contribution beyond neuron localization. The strongest novelty is the expert-versus-neuron stabilization result; broader claims of natural modularity remain contingent on the chosen probes and MoE partition.

reviewer_notes: Read all 16 extracted pages, including appendices on significance testing and perturbation. Four primary arXiv records were checked on 2026-08-23. Numerical claims are transcribed from the paper; causal interpretations are qualified because perturbation operators differ between T5 and Switch.
